blocks.text: The ABCDE approach is a systematic method of assessing and treating critically ill or injured patients. Treat life-threatening problems as they are identified, reassessing continuously.

rows: Respiratory rate, SpO₂, chest movement, breath sounds
Pulse, BP, capillary refill, bleeding, perfusion

items.text: A – Ask the patient to speak; inspect the airway.
B – Breathing rate, oxygen saturation and chest examination.
C – Circulation, control haemorrhage, obtain IV access.
D – Disability, neurological assessment and blood glucose.
E – Expose the patient while preventing hypothermia.
Airway obstruction: Open airway, suction, airway adjuncts and advanced airway support when indicated.
Respiratory compromise: Oxygen and ventilatory support according to clinical need.
Shock: Control bleeding, establish access and give appropriate fluids or blood products.

blocks.text: OSCE pearl: Always introduce yourself, assess responsiveness, call for help when required and use a structured ABCDE approach. Do not wait until completing the entire assessment before treating an immediately life-threatening problem.
Shock is a state of circulatory failure resulting in inadequate tissue perfusion and oxygen delivery.

blocks.text: For adults, the usual IM adrenaline dose is 500 micrograms (0.5 mL of 1 mg/mL solution), injected into the anterolateral thigh. Repeat after 5 minutes if there is inadequate response, following the applicable protocol.
Also provide oxygen, IV crystalloid fluids for cardiovascular compromise and inhaled bronchodilators for persistent bronchospasm as indicated.
Exam pearl: IM adrenaline is the first-line treatment. Antihistamines and corticosteroids must not delay adrenaline.
Acute respiratory failure occurs when the respiratory system cannot maintain adequate oxygenation, carbon dioxide elimination, or both.

items.text: Type 1: Hypoxaemic respiratory failure — PaO₂ below 60 mmHg, usually with normal or low PaCO₂.
Type 2: Hypercapnic respiratory failure — PaCO₂ above 45–50 mmHg, usually with respiratory acidosis.

blocks.text: Exam pearl: Type 1 respiratory failure is primarily an oxygenation problem, while Type 2 involves inadequate ventilation and carbon dioxide retention.
This is the most important classification to remember.
Exam pearl: Always consider obstruction in a patient with AKI, especially when there is anuria, urinary retention or a history of prostatic disease.
Metabolic acidosis is characterised by a primary reduction in serum bicarbonate, usually accompanied by a compensatory reduction in PaCO₂.

blocks.text: Exam pearl: Do not induce vomiting routinely in poisoned patients. Activated charcoal is appropriate only in selected circumstances, and corrosive ingestion or an unprotected airway are important contraindications.
